resources.string: Fictional marker remaining after two tubule segments

Start with 100 arbitrary units (a.u.) of marker. After A = 100 × (1 − A ÷ 100). After B = amount after A × (1 − B ÷ 100). A and B are the chosen percentages. Each segment reclaims the difference between what enters and what leaves it. Total reclaimed = 100 − amount after B.

In real kidneys, the epithelium lining the tubules reabsorbs water and solutes. Tubules can pass from the cortex into the medulla and back. Nephron loops vary in depth, and different segments handle water and solutes differently. This model starts with an inert, fictional marker already inside the tubule. A and B are illustrative steps, not specific structures or kidney regions. Neither slider measures regional clearance or any other kidney function metric. The model does not simulate glomerular filtration, secretion, or urine output.
The filled disks show the marker remaining before, between, and after the two model segments.
